profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 78 (Windstream missing-address campaign): added operator level company history and its August 2025 Uniti Group merger, corroborated independently via a redirected former Windstream URL now carrying a Uniti Group copyright. Applied 110 West 7th Street, Tulsa, sourced from convergence of a fresh maximum confidence reverse geocode and a pre-existing, independently researched sibling registry row at essentially the same coordinates.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Windstream traces to Valor Telecom, established in 2000 to acquire GTE Southwest assets divested by Verizon, and to Windstream Corporation itself, formed in 2006 through a spinoff of Alltels landline business merged with Valor. The company expanded through a long series of acquisitions, including CT Communications for 585 million dollars in 2007, D and E Communications for 330 million dollars in 2009, Iowa Telecom for 1.1 billion dollars and NuVox in 2010, Q-Comm for 782 million dollars in 2010, Hosted Solutions for 310 million dollars also in 2010, PAETEC in 2011, EarthLink for 1.1 billion dollars in 2017, and Broadview Networks for 227 million dollars in 2017. Per Wikipedia, a 2019 US District Court ruling found the company had defaulted on bond payments, its stock fell sharply, and it filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy following a 310 million dollar judgment, emerging in 2020 as a privately held company with debt reduced by more than 4 billion dollars. Wikipedia further states that on August 1, 2025 Uniti Group Inc. completed a merger with Windstream, making Windstream a subsidiary of Uniti. This session independently corroborated that relationship: Windstreams own former business grade colocation web address now redirects to a Uniti Group solutions site carrying a 2026 Uniti Group Inc. copyright notice and routing Windstream branded account logins through it, evidence of a genuine current corporate relationship rather than a stale Wikipedia claim. Given the operating brand itself, Windstream and its consumer facing Kinetic brand, appears to continue rather than being retired, this session records Uniti Group as parent company context rather than correcting the operator field. This specific row sits in downtown Tulsa, Oklahoma at coordinates essentially identical to an independently researched sibling row in this registry recorded under a different telecom operator at 110 West 7th Street, Tulsa, OK 74119, a pattern consistent with a shared multi tenant telecom hub building, sometimes called a carrier hotel, housing more than one operators equipment under separate registry entries. This session independently reverse geocoded this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service and received an exact match at the services maximum confidence level for the same building, 110 West 7th Street. Given this convergence of an independent prior research pass and a fresh, coordinate based reverse geocode, both arriving at the same downtown Tulsa address, this session applies that address to this row.

reading.body:
Windstream operates a facility at 110 West 7th Street in downtown Tulsa, a shared telecommunications hub building. The facility publishes no megawatt capacity figure. Without published power specifications, IT density assumptions, or interconnection details, the site cannot be evaluated for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities and zero published megawatt figures across the state. Windstream's Tulsa location ranks first by published capacity only because no other facility in the state has disclosed power specifications. This reflects absence of data rather than infrastructure significance.

Windstream is now a subsidiary of Uniti Group following an August 2025 merger. Whether this downtown Tulsa address hosts AI-relevant colocation, edge compute, or remains primarily a legacy carrier hotel serving general telecommunications tenancy cannot be determined from published specifications. The absence of power disclosure is typical across Oklahoma's mapped facilities and suggests limited transparency around data center buildout in the state.
